exposure: Successful external cephalic version vs. persistent breech presentation
outcome: Frequency of successful external cephalic version
Predictors of successful external cephalic version
Maternal outcomes (cesarean delivery, endometritis, sepsis, length of stay > 7 days, chorioamnionitis)
cohort: Women with breech presentations at term delivery admissions in the United States between 1998 and 2011 (n=1,079,576)
finding: Successful external cephalic version was associated with a significant reduction in cesarean delivery and several measures of maternal morbidity, but it was performed in a low proportion of women with breech presentation.
mod_finding: Successful external cephalic version in women with breech presentation was associated with a significant reduction in cesarean delivery rates and some measures of maternal morbidity.
